To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 10 min anoxia insult results in downregulation of PKC isoform expression, and magnesium treatment improves recovery after an anoxic insult by blocking the loss of PKCs and by inducing a transient translocation to the membrane fraction of PKCα, PKCβ and PKCε.
a transient anoxic insult did not result in the downregulating of the PKC isoforms.
a 2-min anoxia did not cause a downregulation of PKC, but a 10-min anoxic insult did.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of magnesium on PKC isoforms in rat hippocampi after anoxia.
the mechanisms of magnesium neuroprotective effects on the recovery of synaptic function and PKC downregulatory response in the rat hippocampus.
the mechanisms by which magnesium protects against anoxic transmission damage in hippocampal slices, and we have shown that magnesium blocks the downregulation and translocation of PKCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PKC downregualtion is a late phenomenon that is not a cause of synaptic damage but is rather a consequence of synaptic damage.
magnesium neuroprotection is associated with the prevention of the loss of PKCs and the translocation of PKCs.
the PKC response is a good predictor of synaptic damage and that magnesium treatment improves the PKC response and preserves synaptic function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
magnesium is a potent neuroprotection agent that blocks PKC downregulations and results in a transient translocaton of PKCα to the membrane fraction.
magnesium is a potent neuroprotection agent against synaptic transmission damage during cerebral anoxi and reoxygenati.
magnesium is an effective neuroprotective agent in the anoxic rat hippocampal brain slice model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnesium is a potent neuro-protective agent against anoxic transmission damage in the rat hippocampus.
magnesium is an effective neuroprotectant that preserves synaptic transmission and PKC activity in a model of cerebral anoxia/reoxygenation.
magnesium treatment prevents the downregulation and translocation of PKCs after anoxia and that this is correlated with the preservation of synaptic transmission.
